summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with embedded firmware experience across STM32, Raspberry Pi, and NVIDIA Jetson. Proficient in bare-metal C and direct memory-mapped register programming — the same model as ASIC/SoC driver development — with FreeRTOS, UART/I2C/SPI/GPIO/ADC, and hardware-level debug using logic analyzers and oscilloscopes.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team; owned PCB fabrication, board bring-up, and embedded firmware integration across national-level competitions.
Designed custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE; validated UART and I2C bus timing using logic analyzers and oscilloscopes; implemented closed-loop sensor feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Configured peripherals via direct memory-mapped register writes (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on Cortex-M4 — same programming model as ASIC/SoC vendor register maps.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a hand-written I2C driver; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM; validated in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on STM32; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing with interrupt-driven UART command parsing and PWM servo control.
Deployed YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson for real-time detection; routed control commands to STM32 over UART at ~30 Hz.

projects.name: COFFIN — Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm, RIT Capstone
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via TCA9548A I2C mux; implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++ driving five servos with range-gated contact detection.
Resolved 11 integration failures through systematic firmware validation; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s latency with TensorRT YOLO at ~18 FPS.

projects.name: ABB RobotStudio Automation Simulation
bullets: Programmed in RAPID with TCP socket-based pose acquisition and interrupt-driven press-bench logic; validated full-cycle motion repeatability across a complete assembly pipeline.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
